get.description:
Who is signed in. Always answers: `user` is null without a session, and `auth` lists the
sign-in providers.

put.description: Work in another of one's organisations (kept in the session).

get.description:
The pending invitations sent to the caller's email, only when the provider verified it
(none otherwise), leaving out the organisations they are already in.

post.description: A new organisation, owned by its creator, who now works in it.

delete.description: An owner removes a member; anyone may leave (their own user id). The last owner stays.

get.description: The invitations nobody has accepted yet, unexpired (owners only).

post.description:
An invitation link to copy and send (no email goes out). The link is what lets someone
in, whatever account they sign in with; inviting the same address again gives the same link.

get.description: What an invitation link is for, signed in or not (the token is the secret).

post.description:
Join the organisation of an invitation link while signed in; it becomes the one the
session works in.

get.description:
Every organisation, oldest first, those nobody joined yet included: members and roles,
how many projects it holds.

put.description:
Give a project to another organisation: its members see it from now on, the old one's do
not. Nothing else changes (files, versions, listing sets, share link). 404 for an unknown
project or organisation, 409 while a job is not over; the same organisation changes nothing.

get.description:
The read-only view behind a share link (#24): the scene (current or pinned version),
its renders and photos, all under the link's own paths (/shared/<token>/…, readable signed
out). Nothing that could change the project, nothing the owner wrote.

The projects of the organisation the caller works in (every organisation's for the
read-only token).

post.description:
Add a plan document later (the extension drawings, a survey). The next run sees it;
when documents disagree the builder trusts the most recent one for today's state.

Create (or return) the read-only public link of the project (#24). Optionally pin a
version; sharing again with another version keeps the same token and re-pins it.

delete.description: Revoke the public link: the URL stops working immediately.

patch.description:
Set the project's run settings (model, effort, critic rounds, step budget, in-loop
render quality). Unset fields keep the .env defaults. A running job is not affected: it
took its snapshot at start.

get.description:
What a run started now would use (the stored settings over the .env defaults, effort
values mapped onto the provider).

Rough duration and cost of the next run of `kind`, from this project's finished runs
of that kind (or a typical profile before the first) and the price table.

post.description:
Read the plan set before building (projects without photos): what the house is as
drawn, which sheet is what, and the questions the drawings cannot answer.

Build from scratch. The optional body carries the owner's answers to the intake's
questions (and any notes): they are added to the project's brief for this and every
later pass, and shown as the request that started the build.

Ask for a change, optionally with photographs of the detail to change, and optionally
together with the review findings of the current version: one request, one job.

One message of the conversation (#35): the assistant answers, asks back, makes a small
change itself, or hands a bigger one to the builder (now, or once the running job ends).
It may be sent while the builder works; one answer at a time.

Build the interior of the current scene from the floor plans: rooms, partitions, doors,
furniture and lights, checked against the plan sheets (#33).
Send the stored review findings of a version to the builder as a modification.

Stop a running job. It ends `cancelled` (never resumed); the scene working copy keeps
what the builder had written so far, restore a version to discard it.

get.description: Swiss addresses and parcels matching the text (geo.admin.ch), in LV95.

post.description:
Fetch the terrain, the aerial photo and the buildings around the place (10 to 30 s). Replaces
earlier surroundings; the viewer shows them in the Final and Ultra looks, never the builder.

patch.description: Where the scene sits in its surroundings (the alignment editor).

get.description: The report's settings (prices, weights, attributions…) and what fills the blanks.

put.description: Save the report's settings (the whole set: what is left out goes back to its default).

get.description: The project's listing photo sets: which versions have one, and one set in listing order.

parameters.name: version

schema.description: the version's set (default: the newest set)
schema.title: Version

parameters.description: the version's set (default: the newest set)

post.description:
Shoot a saved version's interior photo set on the photo service (a few minutes, run beside
the scene's own jobs). `reuse` keeps the cameras of the version's last set.

get.description: The version's listing photos in one ZIP, named in listing order with their captions.

The renderer snapshots a scene can be drawn with (newest first, the working copy last),
which one the build path is pinned to and which one the viewer shows by default.

What a project without run settings of its own runs with (the server's .env defaults),
for the settings sheet of a project not created yet.

The models the provider's API offers now, newest first (the .env provider when none is
given). Cached for ten minutes; when the provider cannot be asked the list is empty and
`error` says why.
